### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **72** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**40** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5b3a103c4a67baeadcb214913cd971b5f33dfbc7` — the merge of head `d990af409b7471abae9a5291bb34d81dcaffcd3b` into base `82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5b3a103c4a67baeadcb214913cd971b5f33dfbc7 && git checkout 5b3a103c4a67baeadcb214913cd971b5f33dfbc7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 d990af409b7471abae9a5291bb34d81dcaffcd3b && git checkout -B drift-repro 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 && git merge --no-ff d990af409b7471abae9a5291bb34d81dcaffcd3b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a808f407530fbe86127f7bd40224c9c6e7d9bf06`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/direct-sign-in.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-route-ledger.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts, ui/packages/auth/src/types.ts, ui/packages/auth/src/LoginForm.tsx, ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/LoginPage.tsx, ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/directSignIn.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/ssoCallbackRefusal.ts

PR #33221 on card #33183. Read for this record: the card body and its eight comments (rulings 8 and 10 and D-2 as relayed in 6870716068); the PR body, its 39 files and the net diff `origin/main...a808f407` (merge base `67274aca`); the files at this head and the code they cite on the live tree; the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built, run or re-run. The rest of the diff (tests, locales, generated references, changeset and docs prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs on this head, last read 2026-11-14T14:48Z (all complete): 68 runs, 59 `success`, 9 `skipped` (opt-in, schedule and queue-only jobs), none failed, none still running. Green include Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Type Check UI, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Test Core (8 shards and the roll-up) and Test UI (16 shards and the roll-up). The gates are green; the findings below are ones no gate on this head reads.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies:

1. `/auth/config` serves `features.directSignIn`, a boolean, always (`false` unless the setting is on). Widening. Right: classified in the registry and declared in the response schema.
2. `/auth/config` serves `features.localSignIn` (`hidden` or `off`) while the setting is on. Widening. Right: registered as a non-flag key.
3. `AuthFeaturesConfigSchema` gains two optional members (`authorable-surface/api.json` +2). A response schema, not an authorable key. Right.
4. `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES` gains `directSignIn`, so `requiresFeature` accepts `'directSignIn'` on an action, an action param and an object field group. An accept-set widening for metadata authors, so `Metadata-protocol: added` is right. The mid-registry insertion only reorders how the enum is listed.
5. `GET /api/v1/auth/sign-in/direct`, a new public route while the setting is on, with the closed query set `callbackURL` (once), ledgered `public`. Right as declared. Wrong in one respect: its mount and its advertisement can disagree (F1).
6. `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER['@objectstack/plugin-auth']` gains `NOT_FOUND`. A widening of the published error-code face. Wrong code (F3).
7. `AuthPluginOptions.directSignIn`, `AuthManagerOptions.directSignIn`, the exported `DirectSignInOptions` and `DirectSignInLocalPath`, and four public `AuthManager` methods. Widening. Right.
8. Three environment variables. New inputs; the boot refusal for an off-vocabulary local path applies to a new input only, so nothing is narrowed. Right (see N5).
9. `@object-ui/auth`: `AuthPublicConfig.features` gains both keys; `LoginForm` hides every local way in under `localSignIn: 'off'`. Reachable only with the new server value, so not a narrowing of a published accept set. Right.
10. Console `/login` reads `local` and `direct`, treats `error` as a hold while the flag is on, and navigates to the door. New behaviour behind the flag. Right. Four copy keys in 11 locales.
11. Nothing is narrowed. With the option and the environment unset every answer is as on `main` apart from `directSignIn: false`.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/33183-sso-direct-redirect.md` takes `minor` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@object-ui/auth`, `@object-ui/console` and `@object-ui/i18n`: every package the diff moves, all in one fixed group. The kind is `added`, which takes at least `minor`; the level matches what the diff publishes. `Check Changeset` is `success`.

The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line stands at the start of a line in the PR body and in the changeset, and it is right: the diff widens (items 1 to 10) and narrows nothing (item 11). `Metadata-protocol: added` stands on both and is right (item 4). No BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed.

Owed on the PR body and absent: the `Skills-docs:` line that a kind other than `none` takes (N9).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 6872305139: `open_questions` is empty and `security_findings` is `none`. This review made no security finding.
- Its one `out_of_scope_findings` entry is the review itself, answered by this record. The tier it names is wrong: the PR body, the report and release comment 6872893161 say `TIER_DEFAULT`, but the committed tree carries three published-schema paths, so the face is schema and the tier is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.
- Claim flag, "local sign-in off is decided on the page only; a server-side refusal waits for the ruling text". The text arrived in 6870716068. Ruling 10 puts "no local password for anyone" and the invalidation in the cloud (cloud#4471); D-2 drops the recovery link. The framework's `off` is the page's choice and the schema says so. Answered, and consistent with the rulings as relayed. Until cloud#4471 lands, a hosted password still signs in through the API door.
- Claim flag, "the OAuth client hand-off is not redirected". Answered: consistent with "API keys, MCP and the API are unaffected".
- Claim flag, "the return path is kept only when it is a same-origin relative path". Verified in ④.
- The claim and both amendments still say `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body and the changeset say `added`, which is right. The card's line is stale.
- The PR author is the relay account. No governed path is in the file list (Governed Surface Queue Guard: `success`).
- Escalated to the maintainer, found here and answered by no ruling on the card:
  - E1. What an explicit sign-out does while direct sign-in is on (F2). Hosted turns this on by default.
  - E2. Whether the vendor's default sign-in limit is the right one for an automatic start (F4).

### ④ Design judgment

**`hits` files**

- `packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts`. Holds against ruling 8 as relayed (one flag for the redirect, one value for the configurable local path, with exactly the two states the ruling names) and against its first consumers, `decideDirectSignIn` and `LoginForm`. Both members are optional, so an older server still parses. Its `directSignIn` sentence, "on and able to start", is the contract F1 breaks. N1 on the `localSignIn` sentence.
- `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`. Does not hold against its own header (F3).
- `packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts`. Holds: the entry has the shape of `sso` and `ssoEnforced` (login surface, opt-in, exempt), lowers to `features.directSignIn == true`, and `localSignIn` is rightly a non-flag key. N1 on its jsdoc.

**Implementing files**

- `direct-sign-in.ts`. Agrees with its contract on the setting (environment wins field by field; an off-vocabulary local path throws), on the provider choice, on the closed query set, and on "it mints nothing": the start carries no cookie and no `authorization`, goes to the vendor entry and never back through the route table, and the answer is `302` with `cache-control: no-store` and the vendor's state cookie. Findings F3, F4, N3, N4.
- `auth-manager.ts`. `getPublicConfig()` serves the flag and the value as the registry says; `isDirectSignInUsable()` fails toward showing the page; the constructor refuses an off-vocabulary value at boot. The jsdoc of `AuthManagerOptions.directSignIn` is false for a manager whose plugin was not given the option (F1).
- `auth-plugin.ts`. The `/config` refinement agrees. The mount does not (F1).
- `auth-route-ledger.ts`, `index.ts`. Agree. N6.
- `ui/packages/auth/src/types.ts`. Agrees, except N1.
- `ui/packages/auth/src/LoginForm.tsx`. Agrees: under `localSignIn: 'off'` no email, phone, code, sign-up link or break-glass link is drawn in any state of the form, enforced-SSO mode included, and nothing is painted before the config answers.
- `ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/LoginPage.tsx`, `directSignIn.ts`, `ssoCallbackRefusal.ts`. The decision table and the loop guard agree with the contract. Findings F2, F4, N2, N8.

**Tried and held**

- Open redirect through the return path. The kept path must begin with one slash at each of three decoding layers and is composed onto the canonical origin, so the vendor's redirect stays on the origin by construction. Not broken (N4 is hardening).
- Redirect loop. Every automatic start requires the return mark to be absent, and every return carries it. An identity-provider error, a return without a session, and a door that cannot start all hold the page. Not broken. Sign-out is one bounce, not a loop (F2).
- The local path reopening under `off` (ruling 10, D-2). `?local=1` is ignored; the hand-off and the no-provider states draw the form with no local way in; a failed config read replaces the form; the dev-admin row is gated. On hosted the sign-up prompts cannot appear, because a cloud-managed environment forces sign-up off. Not broken on the sign-in page (N2 on the wording).
- API, MCP and bearer requests. The diff adds one `GET` route and no middleware; nothing else answers with a redirect. Not broken.
- The setting-off CONTROL. With the option and the environment unset the door is not mounted and the page, the form and `/auth/config` are as on `main` apart from `directSignIn: false`. Holds.

**Findings**

**F1 · must-fix · the door is mounted from one source and advertised from another.** `auth-plugin.ts` mounts the door when `resolveDirectSignIn(this.options.directSignIn, env).enabled` (line 3982), the plugin's constructor options, written once. `/auth/config` serves `features.directSignIn` and `localSignIn` from `AuthManager.directSignInSetting()`, which reads `this.config.directSignIn` (auth-manager.ts 5937 to 5939): the draft that `init()` hands the manager after `auth:configure` handlers have mutated it (auth-plugin.ts 758, 882, 942), and later whatever `applyConfigPatch` merges. So a `directSignIn` that arrives through `auth:configure`, or through `applyConfigPatch`, is served as `directSignIn: true` with its `localSignIn`, while no door is mounted on either route table. `auth:configure` is the hook this plugin and `plugin-lifecycle-events.ts` document for packages that contribute auth providers, hosted control-plane SSO among them, and under `objectstack serve`, whose `new AuthPlugin` passes no `directSignIn`, it is the only way in besides the environment. The Console then replaces the sign-in page with the vendor's 404 on every signed-out visit, and with `localSignIn: 'off'` the page offers nothing else. Nothing says so at boot. This contradicts the schema sentence ("on and able to start"), the registry's `refined to "able to start"`, the route's own comments ("the same inputs the manager resolves it from", "navigates only to a door that starts a sign-in"), the jsdoc of `AuthManagerOptions.directSignIn`, and AGENTS.md route rule 4 (mount everything advertised). Commit 6a155822 moved the read from the manager to the plugin option because route-table fakes carry a partial manager; the neighbouring mounts feature-detect the manager instead. Same class, smaller: the manager reads the environment live and the mount reads it once. Fix: one source for both, and a pin through `init()` with an `auth:configure` handler that sets `directSignIn`, asserting that the door answers 302 and `/auth/config` advertises it.

**F2 · should-fix · an explicit sign-out is signed straight back in.** `AuthProvider.signOut()` clears the user and raises `sessionEndedBySignOut`; `LoginRedirect` then sends the tab to `/login` with no query. `decideDirectSignIn` sees a plain signed-out visit and answers `start`; `LoginPage` never reads `sessionEndedBySignOut`. Provider logout exists only for a `sys_sso_provider` row whose switch is on; for an `oidcProviders` entry, `objectstack-cloud` included, the provider session survives, so the person who pressed Sign out is back in the Console without a click. `createAuthClient.signOut` already names this hazard for the one-click case. The page, the tests and the docs do not speak of sign-out. Ruling 8 speaks of an unauthenticated visit, not of a person who has just left, so the behaviour is the maintainer's to state (E1): hold the page after an explicit sign-out (the flag is in `useAuth()`, the retry card is already drawn), or record that the bounce is intended. Pin whichever it is.

**F3 · should-fix · the new ledger row registers a synonym the ledger tells authors not to register.** `runDirectSignIn` answers the off-at-request-time case with `404 NOT_FOUND` (direct-sign-in.ts:332), and the diff adds `NOT_FOUND` under `@objectstack/plugin-auth`. `NOT_FOUND` is a grandfathered synonym of the standard member `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (`STANDARD_SYNONYM_WAIVERS`, whose reason lists its emitters and not this one). The ledger header (lines 63 to 65) says a generic not-found uses the standard catalog, and every other 404 this package emits is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, which needs no row. The provenance gate flagged the stamp; the row was added where the stamp should have changed. A registered code is published face and cannot be renamed later without a break. Fix: stamp `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, drop the row, and drop its mention from the PR body.

**F4 · should-fix · a rate-limited start is reported as a misconfigured provider.** The door re-dispatches the vendor start with the caller's address, so the vendor's sign-in limiter counts it. better-auth 1.7.12's default rule for paths under `/sign-in` is 3 per 10 seconds per address, or one shared bucket where no client address is established, wherever the limiter is on (its production default). plugin-auth writes no custom rule for `/sign-in/social` or `/sign-in/sso`, and neither vendor plugin overrides it. With direct sign-in every arrival at `/login` is a start, where before only a click was. The fourth arrival from one address in the window (an office behind one egress address, a link a team opens together) gets a non-200, which the door folds into `start_refused`. The `warn` line says `start_refused` and the page says "Single sign-on could not be started for this system. Ask your administrator to check which sign-in service it uses." Wrong reason and wrong advice, on a path ordinary load reaches once hosted has this on by default. Fix: tell a 429 apart, with its own reason, code and copy. The limit itself is E2.

**Nits** (no effect on correctness or on the contract of rulings 8 and 10)

- N1. `localSignIn` is served whenever the setting is on, including when `directSignIn` is served `false` because no provider can start; `LoginForm` relies on exactly that. The schema description and the registry jsdoc say "served only while direct sign-in is on", and `types.ts` says "while `directSignIn` is on", which names the flag and is false in that state. Say "while the setting is on, whatever `directSignIn` reads".
- N2. The changeset, the docs and a `LoginPage.tsx` comment say the page (the docs table: "the Console") draws no local way in and no sign-up "in any state". The form does not. The page still draws `InvitationSignUpPrompt` and `FirstOwnerPrompt` when the server offers sign-up, and `/register` and `/forgot-password` are outside this diff. Hosted is unaffected (sign-up is forced off there). Narrow the sentence to the sign-in form on the prose faces.
- N3. The door spells its two refusal sentences by hand. `invitation-preview.ts` in the same package uses `unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage` and `repeatedQueryParamMessage` from `@objectstack/rest`, whose header says one sentence for every route. Code and status agree; only the words differ.
- N4. The return-path check judges the spelling as sent; the path the URL parser resolves is judged for its origin only. Same-origin holds by construction. Judging the resolved path as well would make the check independent of how the server routes what it receives. Hardening only.
- N5. `OS_AUTH_LOCAL_SIGN_IN` does nothing unless direct sign-in is on, and set alone it is inert without a word at boot. Its name does not group under `OS_AUTH_DIRECT_SIGN_IN_*`. An environment variable name is hard to change after release.
- N6. `AuthRouteLedgerEntry.requires` is documented as "better-auth plugin this route needs"; the new row names a setting. The row's comment says so; the field's jsdoc does not.
- N7. `sign-in-method-floor.ts` and the boot report count "email and password on" as a way in, mirroring what the sign-in page offers. Under `localSignIn: 'off'` the page no longer offers it, so deleting the last identity provider passes the floor and leaves the page with "No sign-in method is available". Outside this diff, and on hosted the provider is not deletable. A reproducible defect in a neighbouring guard: owed a follow-up card, not a wider PR.
- N8. The IP allow-list exempts `/config` so that a blocked client still gets a clean page, but the door is a top-level navigation and is not exempt, so a blocked client now lands on the raw `403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED` body. After an identity-provider error, the retry also loses `?redirect=`, because the error return address is the bare `/login`. Follow-up.
- N9. PR-body lines: the `Skills-docs:` line owed by `Metadata-protocol: added` is absent (the skills name `requiresFeature` without listing its values; the generated references carry the new value); the body names the wrong review tier; its Verification section is pinned to `f690739f`, one commit behind this head.

A must-fix is on record, so the verdict is FAIL. F1 to F4 each earn a delta review of their fix. The nits ride on the prose faces, as follow-up cards, or with that fix.

(Deviation: the sub-agent wrote the record to scratch and the seat thread posted it verbatim through the relay, since the sub-agent holds no relay write.)

  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them (named at least: plugin-auth `auth-manager.ts`, `direct-sign-in.ts`, `auth-plugin.ts`, `auth-route-ledger.ts`; `@object-ui/auth` `types.ts`, `LoginForm.tsx`; Console `LoginPage.tsx`, `directSignIn.ts`) — reviewed for agreement with the contract.

  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY; code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs on the head already answered every derived gate family. If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.

Judge, in the record's own sections: ① Derived judgments; ② Semver level; ③ Boundary flags; ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file and EVERY implementing file, and try to break the design (open redirect through the return path, a redirect loop, the local path reopening while `localSignIn` is `off` against ruling 10 and D-2, API/MCP/bearer requests being redirected, the setting-off CONTROL). Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit. ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with the adopting card-thread session.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
